did_you_know.text: Did you know? Zedekiah reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years, and his mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
Did you know? The Babylonian siege of Jerusalem began in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day; the Babylonian army built a siege rampart around the city.
Did you know? In the eleventh year of Zedekiah’s reign, the famine in Jerusalem became so severe that there was no bread for the people of the land.
Did you know? After the city was breached, the soldiers left Jerusalem at night through a gate between the walls and tried to escape along the road to the Arabah.
Did you know? At Riblah, the king of Babylon executed Zedekiah’s sons and the leaders of Judah in his presence, and then blinded him.
Did you know? In the fifth month, on the tenth day, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuzaradan arrived in Jerusalem and led the destruction.
Did you know? The Chaldeans broke apart and carried to Babylon the bronze furnishings of the temple, including the bronze pillars, the bronze Sea, and the stands.
Did you know? Each of the two bronze pillars was eighteen cubits high, with a bronze capital five cubits high on top.
Did you know? The chapter states that there were one hundred pomegranates in all around the latticework, of which ninety-six were on the outside of the pillars.
Did you know? After thirty-seven years in exile, Jehoiachin was released by Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, who brought him out of prison and gave him a place of honor among the kings in Babylon.
